explanation: I found no Lie-module version of this result in Mathlib. The closest declaration is `LinearMap.isCompl_of_proj` in `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Projection.lean`, together with its relatives `LinearMap.IsProj.isCompl` (same file) and the group-representation lemma in `Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Maschke.lean`. All of these work with plain submodules, not Lie submodules. The library's proof uses `isCompl_of_proj`, but it first has to build an equivariant Lie module map, restrict its codomain to `N`, take its kernel as a Lie submodule, and move back and forth between Lie submodules and submodules. That is more than the routine glue allowed for `special_case`. I grepped `Mathlib/Algebra/Lie` for `IsCompl`, `isCompl_of_proj`, `proj` and `exists_isCompl`, and none of the hits is a statement about equivariant projections.
